answer_1.quote: we collect and analyze a new dataset of openended responses from both humans and LLMs to identical social scenarios, enabling direct comparison of politeness strategies.
datasets: new dataset of open-ended responses from humans and LLMs
answer_1.outputs: open-ended responses in English social scenarios involving feedback on performances or creative work

answer_2.quote: We report Spearman correlation and mean squared error (MSE) between LLM and human responses as an overall measure of fit

answer_3.quote: We used LLMs (GPT-4.1 and Claude-3.7-Sonnet) as annotators, following best practices. Annotations were manually verified and corrected where necessary.

answer_4.quote: We conducted a two-alternative forced-choice evaluation with 156 human evaluators, each viewing four different scenarios. Evaluators made five judgments per scenario
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators made five judgments per scenario: (1) comparing human vs. LLM responses, (2-3) comparing goal-congruent vs. goal-incongruent responses for both sources, and (4-5) comparing rating-congruent vs. rating-incongruent responses for both sources.
criteria: preference between human and LLM responses
